requirements.quote: One GitHub client per schedd: single GraphQL query per pass for all issues in the batch (state, labels, milestone, comment count, updatedAt), ETag/`If-None-Match` for the rest, results cached with a TTL; `gh` subprocesses only for writes.
`lane.unresolved` from a network error becomes `gh.unavailable` (already uncapped, 60 s) and serves the last good cache; never a lane failure.
Priority and `nice` for subprocesses; a per-pass budget of subprocess spawns, logged.
Optional: allow the dispatcher to run on a non-workstation host (Legion WSL) when `orchestrate.dispatcher_host` is set.
requirements.why: Marked optional in the issue; a separate placement feature, independent of the read layer.

requirements.quote: Test: a pass over 200 issues performs at most 2 GraphQL calls and 0 per-issue `gh` spawns when nothing changed.
Test: GitHub unreachable for 15 min yields no `lane.unresolved` rows and no lost admissions; cached data used.
`event loop stalled > 5 s` count under load test of 20 lanes: 0.
requirements.evidence: bin/lean/schedd-load.test.mjs is the existing load harness; stall count is measured from schedd.log on the host. In-lane, R5 bounds the spawns that cause the stalls.

requirements.quote: Idle free-lane minutes attributed to `dispatch-stalled` fall to near zero in the efficiency ledger.
requirements.why: Only measurable from the efficiency ledger on the production host after the change runs under real load.

requirements.quote: A transient network error on the host is classified as a lane problem and each issue pays a 120-240 s requeue.

Per-issue GitHub reads are spawned as one `gh` subprocess each (milestone, state, comments, labels) from several loops (orchestrate dispatch, hold/needs-human watcher `orchestrate.mjs:1756`, dependency checks, health, lane start `lean.mjs`), with no shared cache, no conditional requests and no batching.
requirements.why: adapt: scope to the dispatcher path (lane resolution, label/view reads, held-root watcher); lean.mjs lane-start reads already use a per-run gh cache and stay unchanged.

deliverables.change: New schedd GitHub read client: injectable io.gh; one GraphQL call per refresh for all batch issues (state, labels, milestone, comment count, updatedAt), chunked to cap calls; TTL cache serving the last good value when gh fails; isNetworkError(err) classifier; spawn counter with a per-pass budget and log line; gh invoked under nice.
New tests: 200 issues cost at most 2 GraphQL calls and 0 per-issue spawns when unchanged; 15 min of network failure serves cache; isNetworkError; budget log.
resolveLane: a network error on the milestone read returns a gh.unavailable result (not lane.unresolved); reads go through the reader when supplied.
Add a case: network error gives gh.unavailable, a non-network error still gives lane.unresolved.
Create one reader per schedd and route labelNames, viewOf, the milestone pre-read and makeDispatchCheck through it; refresh once per pass for the batch's issues.
Held-root watcher and retryLane use cached reads; a gh.unavailable lane result defers uncapped at 60 s without a lane failure and without losing the admission.
Add a test: GitHub unreachable (fake clock, 15 min) yields no lane.unresolved rows and no lost admissions.
Wrap the dispatcher read gh with nice and count spawns through the reader.
Document that GH_UNAVAILABLE is also used for the dispatcher read path (comment only, if needed).

preserve.what: resolveLane result shape and the non-network transient lane.unresolved retry (bin/lean/lane.mjs:75-90).
lean.mjs lane-start reads keep their per-run gh cache (bin/lean/lean.mjs:411) and are unchanged.
makeDispatchCheck semantics: a closed issue or merged feat/issue-N-lean PR ends the row (bin/engine-cli.mjs:2565).
Writes (labels, comments, PRs) still go through gh subprocesses (bin/lean/effects.mjs:495).

regression.covers: orchestrate.mjs callers of issueLabels, dispatchCheck and retryLane

decisions.choice: Batch reads with one GraphQL call via `gh api graphql` and a TTL cache, instead of per-issue ETag requests.
decisions.justification: A single chunked query makes the 200-issues-in-at-most-2-calls criterion testable; the existing per-run gh cache (bin/lean/effects.mjs:461) cannot serve a long-lived schedd.

decisions.choice: Reuse the existing GH_UNAVAILABLE code rather than adding a new outcome code.
decisions.justification: bin/engine/outcome-codes.mjs:43 already defines it, and the issue names it.
